Answers a prompt on the user's behalf: action. This is the ONE item on the board where the DO reading was actually applied - its own note says access 35 because 'going to the tab to answer a prompt is something a normal user can already do quickly'. Right axis, right direction; if anything 35 is generous, since switching to a pane and typing is something this user does dozens of times a day, which puts it nearer 20. Not wrong.

Navigates for the user (focuses the terminal): action. Board reads 28, which is about where the DO reading lands - hunting the right pane among 3-12 costs seconds, not minutes. The number is right; the reasoning is not, since the note derives 28 from 'the cheap half of B4' rather than from what the user does today. Not wrong.
Reveals elapsed block time. Information.

A queue is a rendering of facts the user cannot assemble (which of my twelve are blocked); the answering it enables is B4. Read as an action instead - deliberately sweeping every pane and clearing gates in one pass - the DO score is also ~50, so 58 survives either reading. Not flagged.

Routes a request into another system's state: action. Doing it by hand today means spotting the review in a pane and filing the gate yourself, which is multi-step and Spacedock-specific: ~50. Board's 50 coincides. Category wrong, number right.

The stage display already shipped; what is left is a user-declared tripwire that writes a condition and fires on it: action. No harness or dashboard lets a user declare that line today - the manual equivalent is polling Spacedock state files with a script, which a normal user will not do: ~78. Board's 80 is right, but for a reason its own note contradicts (the note argues 'moderate' on information grounds and then scores 80). Number right, reasoning wrong.

WRONG, and it is the clearest miscategorisation on the board. This does the triage for the user and lands as a persisted default ('make it the default, and bring it to both display modes'), so it is an action. Calm mode's attention sort already ships - the capability exists behind a toggle, so DOING this today costs one click: ~12. Scored 72, which puts a shipped-behind-a-toggle default in the differentiated corner alongside C2 and D5 and overstates its access by roughly 60 points. The genuinely hard information ('which of my twelve needs me most') belongs to B7/D1; D7 is only the ordering.
Reveals an inferred attribute. Information.

Suppresses notifications on the user's behalf: action, and a settings write. The coarse version is available today in two clicks (OS Do Not Disturb, or close the tab), and only the selective part - everything except your-call - is out of reach: ~25. Board's 20 lands right. Category wrong, number right.
Reveals what happened while away. Information.

Delivers a message to another device: action. Nothing a normal user can assemble - the briefing is explicit that no harness pushes off the machine, so the manual path is building a bridge yourself: ~85. Board's 75 is understated by about ten points but sits in the right band, so not wrong. Note the axis is doing double duty here: H2 is not a fact at all, it is a channel, and its value is that it makes D4/D5/D6 reach a user who took the product's advice and left.

Reveals branch and PR state. Information; a user can run `git branch` and `gh pr list`, which is what 45 encodes.
Writes user state (a dismissal) on the user's behalf: action. The equivalent today is closing the tab, which is free: ~10. Board's 15 lands right. Category wrong, number right.

WRONG, and the board's own note contains the disproof. This asks the session for a summary and hands the user a prompt - it types into a session, so it is an action - and the note records the user already performing the whole ritual by hand: 'I will pause the job, ask for a summary of what has been done, and get a prompt I can give a follow-up session.' A sentence the user types into a pane they are already looking at is near the floor: ~15. Scored 62, which is a measure of how hard it is to KNOW the wall is coming (that is A1's 12, plus the projection in A5) rather than how hard the hand-off is to perform. The item's real scarcity is A1 and the DEC-2 slice, both of which are already priced elsewhere (requires: A1; build 70).

The revealed fact is 'these four are one project', which is information. The proposal half is action-shaped - drafting a workflow the user could draft themselves with a commission flow, ~50 - and the board's 55 covers that reading too, so no flag.

Board's 55 overstates it slightly but sits in the right band, so not wrong. What makes F6 expensive is DEC-2's write path and workflow generation, both already priced in build (90).
